title: Bilio-pancreatic endoscopic ultrasonography for diagnosis of biliary parasitosis
case_text:
A 48-year-old Portuguese woman was admitted at the emergency department for severe upper abdominal pain radiating to the back, without any sign of peritonitis. There was no history of drugs or ethanol abuse, pregnancy test was negative and she had not traveled to any other country in the last 5 years. Abdominal CT scan and laboratory tests were completely normal including blood counts. She was started on analgesics, but seeing no response, a diagnostic biliopancreatic endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS) was planned in order to rule out acute pancreatitis.
Trans-duodenal study showed an 8 mm dilated common bile duct (CBD) containing a long linear triple-layer structure (Fig. 1A), hyperechoic outside and hypoechoic inside, without acoustic shadow. Characteristics of Ascaris lumbricoides were recognized: two classical hyperechoic linear echogenic strips on either side of the longitudinal anechoic (lumen) of the ascaris. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography showed the linear filling defect due to the worm in CBD (Fig. 1B). Sphincterotomy was performed to retrieve a 15-cm long parasite with the help of a Dormia basket (Fig. 1C). In conclusion, bilio-pancreatic EUS may be helpful for diagnosis of upper abdominal pain if other investigations are negative, and triple linear hyper- hypo-hyperechoic tubular structure inside the CBD is a classical presentation of biliary parasitosis, that can be the cause of severe upper abdominal pain even without eosinophilia and travel to an endemic area.

   - STRICTLY EXCLUDE from <case_prompt>:
     * Any mention of the disease name or pathogen genus/species (e.g., do not write "Leptospirosis", "Burkholderia", "Leishmania", "Paragonimus").
     * Confirmatory send-out PCR panels, serological titers, blood culture organism identifications, or biopsy histopathology.
     * The clinical outcome or treatment response (these belong in the diagnostic reasoning, not the presentation).

3. STRUCTURE OF <diagnostic_reasoning>:
   - Enumerate all alternative candidate diagnoses considered in the text.
   - For each candidate, provide a concise summary explaining why it was considered and why it was ruled out in this patient, followed by a direct verbatim quote from the article in quotation marks.
   - Conclude with the Diagnostic Pivot: the pivotal clinical and confirmatory turning point that established the confirmed diagnosis.

4. TARGET CANONICAL DISEASE:
   - The verified ground-truth disease for this patient is: Soil-Transmitted Helminths
   - Disease subtype / specific manifestation: biliary ascariasis
